newsitem.title: INDIA: India copper bounces back as state firm cuts rates.
newsitem.headline: India copper bounces back as state firm cuts rates.

text.p: Indian copper prices bounced back on Wednesday while other base metals were steady amid dull trade, dealers said.

Copper rose by 100 rupees to 12,450 per quintal on thin supplies and shortage of ready stock. State-run Hindustan Copper Ltd cut selling prices by 4,000 rupees per tonne for January but that had little impact in the market, one broker said.
Zinc was steady at 6,400 rupees, lead at 4,450 rupees and aluminium at 7,250 rupees. Tin was available at the previous level of 34,300 rupees and nickel at 36,500 rupees.
